speaker: Doctor
text: I'm sorry to hear you're dealing with these symptoms. To better understand what might be causing your pruritic rash and recent illness, have you noticed if your rash appears in a specific pattern, such as spreading from your trunk to your limbs? Also, did anyone around you recently experience similar symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum). The progression of fever for a week followed by defervescence and the appearance of a pruritic rash sparing the face (or appearing after the fever breaks) in a young child is classic for HHV-6/7 infection. REQUEST IMAGES: No further imaging is required; the clinical presentation is sufficient for diagnosis.
